claim: The QVenture rubric separates deals on disclosed evidence, including business models that have no SaaS metrics.

calibration.note: Reconstructed descriptions of companies with public outcomes, written with hindsight. Measures DISCRIMINATION and RANGE only — never predictive accuracy.
calibration.caveat: These fixtures state almost no figures, so rubric v5's non-SaaS evidence layer never fires on them: the v4 and v5 numbers are identical to the decimal. This harness cannot measure the capability added in v5 — that is what the hard-cases harness is for. The capital-intensive arm has n=1 on the success side and is not a measurement.

hardCases.note: Matched strong/weak pairs inside one sector and stage, so sector priors are held constant and the gap comes only from what the plan discloses.

openIssues: On plans that disclose no figures at all, the composite still compresses into roughly 49-66 of a nominal 0-100 scale. That is defensible (no evidence, no movement) but the scale as presented overstates its own resolution.

No case in the calibration corpus reaches 'invest'. On disclosure-rich input the hard-cases harness does reach it (marketplace strong, 72.6), so the band is reachable — but not on evidence-free descriptions.
Capital-intensive discrimination in the calibration corpus is 1.2 points, on n=1 success. Needs more known-outcome capital-intensive companies before any claim is made about it.
